# Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes

Zihang Fu Affiliation: National University of Singapore
Email: [zihangfu@u.nus.edu](mailto:)    Fanxiao Li Affiliation: Yunnan
University Email: [jiayingwu@u.nus.edu](mailto:)    Jianyang Gu
Affiliation: The Ohio State University    Haonan Wang
Affiliation: National University of Singapore    Preslav Nakov
Affiliation: Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence   
Bryan Hooi Affiliation: National University of Singapore    Min-Yen Kan
Affiliation: National University of Singapore    Jiaying Wu
^(†)^(†)thanks: Corresponding author. Affiliation: National University
of Singapore

###### Abstract

Large Language Model (LLM)-augmented Community Notes offer a scalable
path for timely, evidence-grounded correction of health misinformation
on social platforms. However, they still reset at every post, leaving
useful correction experience from prior cases unused. We introduce
EvoNote, an agentic framework that enables health Community Notes
generation to self-evolve through an evolving experience memory of prior
misinformation correction episodes. Its core is fine-grained credit
assignment: EvoNote grounds trajectory-level feedback in health-specific
note qualities and distills it into action-level memory for claim
analysis, evidence acquisition, and note writing. We evaluate EvoNote on
MM-HealthCN, a 1.2K-instance multimodal benchmark of user-flagged health
posts with human-written Community Notes and crowd-derived helpfulness
labels. Under a human-validated hierarchical utility judge,
EvoNote-generated notes are preferred over corresponding human-written
notes in 89.6% of cases; on a separate set of Needs More Ratings posts
without a crowd helpfulness verdict, EvoNote produces helpful notes for
82.0% of cases. It also reduces the median time needed to produce a
candidate correction from over 13 hours in the human-note pipeline to
under 2 minutes. Analyses link these gains to stronger evidence use and
reusable correction strategies, positioning self-evolving note
generation as a promising paradigm for health misinformation governance.

## 1 Introduction

![Refer to caption](2606.02215v1/intro.png)

Figure 1: Paradigms for LLM-augmented Community Notes generation. (a)
Existing pipelines treat each episode independently. (b) EvoNote
distills prior episodes into evolving memory to improve future notes.

Health misinformation on social platforms requires timely,
evidence-backed, and user-understandable correction [Vraga and Bode
(2020)](#bib.bib19); [Ecker et al. (2022)](#bib.bib17); [Kbaier et al.
(2024)](#bib.bib20). Community Notes [Wojcik et al. (2022)](#bib.bib18)
on X offers a scalable and increasingly influential governance paradigm
for this task, turning crowd-sourced verification and community ratings
into concise, source-grounded corrections that can be shown directly
alongside misleading posts [Renault et al. (2024)](#bib.bib13);
[Slaughter et al. (2025)](#bib.bib21).

LLM-augmented Community Notes [Wu et al. (2025)](#bib.bib1); [Singh et
al. (2026)](#bib.bib2) further improve the timeliness and helpfulness of
correction through automated, evidence-grounded note generation.
However, as shown in
Figure [1](#S1.F1 "Figure 1 ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes"),
current pipelines still follow a one-pass paradigm, treating each post
as an isolated instance. This formulation fits poorly with real-world
health misinformation governance, where misleading claims arrive as a
chronological stream and often recur through similar rhetorical
strategies [Skafle et al. (2022)](#bib.bib22) and evidence needs
[Schneider et al. (2021)](#bib.bib23). Our analysis of 4.9K
health-related notes published over 41 months
(§[3](#S3 "3 Motivating Analysis: Reusable Misinformation Correction Experience ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes"))
confirms this recurrence and shows that it creates reusable correction
experience: earlier helpful notes often reveal transferable
evidence-seeking and writing strategies for later posts of the same
type. Yet under a one-pass formulation, this experience remains
episode-local, leaving later corrections vulnerable to repeated,
avoidable errors. This motivates self-evolving note generation: systems
that turn prior note-generation episodes into reusable experience to
guide future notes.

Motivated by this, we introduce EvoNote, an agentic framework that
enables self-evolving health Community Notes generation through an
evolving experience memory of prior misinformation correction episodes.
For each note-generation trajectory, which spans claim analysis,
evidence acquisition, and note writing, a Social Utility Judge evaluates
the trajectory using four health-specific note qualities grounded in
prior work on health communication: (1) understandability [Sørensen et
al. (2012)](#bib.bib27), (2) meaningfulness for health interpretation
and risk perception [Ferrer and Klein (2015)](#bib.bib30), (3) usability
for safe public action [Denniss et al. (2022)](#bib.bib26), and (4)
trustworthiness under evidence uncertainty [Kington et al.
(2021)](#bib.bib24). A Memory Evolver then distills these judgments into
fine-grained strategies, assigning each lesson to the phase where it can
guide future generation. At inference time, EvoNote retrieves relevant
memories to guide claim analysis, budget-aware web evidence acquisition,
and evidence-grounded note writing without updating model parameters.

To evaluate EvoNote, we curate MM-HealthCN, a 1.2K-instance multimodal
benchmark of consensus-resolved health posts flagged by users, paired
with human-written Community Notes, crowd-derived helpfulness labels,
and a human-validated protocol for hierarchical note utility evaluation
(§[5](#S5 "5 The MM-HealthCN Benchmark ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")).
On MM-HealthCN, offline pairwise evaluation
(§[6.2](#S6.SS2 "6.2 Main Results: Effectiveness of EvoNote ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes"))
shows that EvoNote-generated notes are preferred over the corresponding
human-written Community Notes in 89.6% of cases under a human-validated
utility judge, while also outperforming LLM-augmented Community Notes
baselines. On unresolved Needs More Ratings cases, where crowd consensus
has not yet been reached, EvoNote produces helpful notes for 82.0% of
cases while reducing the median over-13-hour human-note latency to under
2 minutes per case. Further analyses
(§[7](#S7 "7 Discussion ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes"))
link these gains to more diverse and higher-quality evidence sources,
together with reusable memories that encode recurring correction
strategies. These results point to a central design principle for health
misinformation governance: every flagged post should become experience
before the next similar one recurs.

## 2 Related Work

Community Notes and LLM Augmentation. Crowd-sourced fact-checking
provides a scalable response to online misinformation [Allen et al.
(2021)](#bib.bib11); [Martel et al. (2024)](#bib.bib10); [Shahbazi and
Bunker (2024)](#bib.bib9); [Pfänder and Altay (2025)](#bib.bib12); [Xing
et al. (2026)](#bib.bib25), and Community Notes on X has been shown to
reduce misinformation engagement [Chuai et al. (2024b)](#bib.bib41);
[Slaughter et al. (2025)](#bib.bib21) and support balanced discourse
[Chuai et al. (2024a)](#bib.bib42). Its impact, however, depends on
useful notes being written, rated, and surfaced in time [Renault et al.
(2024)](#bib.bib13); [Wu et al. (2025)](#bib.bib1), creating a
bottleneck for health misinformation, where rapid early spread makes
correction delay especially costly [Kouzy et al. (2020)](#bib.bib43);
[Van Der Linden (2022)](#bib.bib44). This bottleneck has motivated LLM
augmentation for note creation, either by aggregating multiple existing
Needs More Ratings notes [De et al. (2025)](#bib.bib3) or by generating
one-pass evidence-grounded notes for individual posts [Wu et al.
(2025)](#bib.bib1); [Singh et al. (2026)](#bib.bib2). The first path
depends on multiple human candidates for the same post; the second
resets after each post. EvoNote fills this gap by turning each agentic
correction trajectory into reusable action-level memory for future note
generation.

Memory-Augmented Agents. Prior work equips LLM agents with experience
reuse through passive memory over retrieved documents, dialogue
histories, or stored facts [Lewis et al. (2020)](#bib.bib46); [Packer et
al. (2024)](#bib.bib48); [Zhong et al. (2024)](#bib.bib47); managed
long-term memory with add, merge, delete, and retrieval operations
[Chhikara et al. (2025)](#bib.bib49); [Rasmussen et al.
(2025)](#bib.bib50); [Li et al. (2025)](#bib.bib51); and
trajectory-based memory that stores reflections, procedural hints, or
reusable plans from prior interactions [Shinn et al.
(2023)](#bib.bib52); [Zhao et al. (2024)](#bib.bib53); [Suzgun et al.
(2026)](#bib.bib54). Recent self-evolving memory work, such as
Evo-Memory [Wei et al. (2025)](#bib.bib15), studies experience reuse
across continuous task streams. EvoNote builds on this direction but
goes beyond retrieving past experience by assigning it to the correction
stage where it should guide action. For health Community Notes
generation, this means distilling trajectory-level feedback into
health-grounded, phase-specific strategies for claim analysis, evidence
acquisition, and note writing. This positions EvoNote as memory-level
self-evolution under a fixed backbone and workflow, complementary to
broader methods that update prompts, workflows, or policies [Wang et al.
(2025)](#bib.bib45); [He et al. (2026)](#bib.bib4).

Figure 2: Reusable misinformation correction experience can remain

## 3 Motivating Analysis: Reusable Misinformation Correction Experience

Health misinformation correction on social platforms unfolds as a
stream, and misleading mechanisms and evidence needs often recur over
time [Skafle et al. (2022)](#bib.bib22). This makes earlier helpful
notes a potential source of reusable correction experience. We analyze
health Community Notes on X to ask two questions: (1) Do misleading
health posts recur through correction-relevant claim patterns? (2) Can
later notes still fail on a pattern that has already received a helpful
correction?

### 3.1 Data and Claim Pattern Extraction

Data Scope. We collect publicly available, user-contributed Community
Notes on X¹¹ 1
[https://x.com/i/communitynotes/download-data](https://x.com/i/communitynotes/download-data)
up to 14 October 2025 and retain English entries for consistency.
Following prior work [Wu et al. (2025)](#bib.bib1), we identify
health-related notes through topic-oriented filtering with Lingshu-32B
[Xu et al. (2025)](#bib.bib5), a medical-specific LLM, and retrieve the
corresponding flagged misleading posts from X. This yields 48,295 notes
addressing 40,116 health-related flagged posts. Among them, 6,336
(13.12%) notes have crowd-derived helpfulness labels (“Helpful”: 4,874;
“Not Helpful”: 1,462); the remaining cases are unresolved, i.e., “Needs
More Ratings”. Full data setup is provided in
Appendix [A.1](#A1.SS1 "A.1 Health-Related Data Filtering ‣ Appendix A Details of Motivating Analysis ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes");
additional latency and visibility statistics are reported in
Appendix [A.3](#A1.SS3 "A.3 Latency and Visibility Statistics ‣ Appendix A Details of Motivating Analysis ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes").

Claim Pattern Extraction. We derive correction-relevant claim patterns
from 4,874 helpful human-written notes published between May 2022 and
October 2025. Helpful notes provide high-precision signals for
misleadingness attribution by revealing what aspect of the post required
correction and what evidence or framing made the correction useful. Two
human experts collaboratively reviewed 200 sampled note-post pairs to
summarize the main correction causes and construct a compact taxonomy of
misleading mechanisms
(Table [4](#A1.T4 "Table 4 ‣ A.3 Latency and Visibility Statistics ‣ Appendix A Details of Motivating Analysis ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")).
We then use GPT-4.1 [OpenAI (2025)](#bib.bib8) to classify the remaining
helpful-note cases under this taxonomy. For posts involving multiple
mechanisms, we assign the primary pattern according to the correction
strategy most central to the helpful note. Detailed category definitions
are provided in
Appendix [A.2](#A1.SS2 "A.2 Claim Pattern Extraction ‣ Appendix A Details of Motivating Analysis ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes").

![Refer to caption](2606.02215v1/overview.png)

Figure 3: Overview of EvoNote for self-evolving health Community Notes
generation. EvoNote turns trajectory-level feedback into evolving
experience memory to inform future note-generation episodes.

### 3.2 Useful Lessons Remain Episode-Local

Our analysis reveals two key observations. (1) Recurring claim patterns
create reusable correction needs. As shown in
Figure [2](#S2.F2 "Figure 2 ‣ 2 Related Work ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")(a),
the cases cluster around correction-relevant patterns, such as medical
mechanism misrepresentations and unsupported causality. These patterns
imply transferable strategies, such as verifying source context,
separating association from causation, and decomposing biomedical
mechanism overclaims. (2) Useful lessons can remain episode-local. In
Figure [2](#S2.F2 "Figure 2 ‣ 2 Related Work ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")(b),
an earlier helpful note exposes a reusable lesson for medical mechanism
overclaims: check quote context, evidence type, and biological
distinctions. However, later notes for similar posts miss this lesson,
leaving the mechanism claim under-addressed or over-narrowly rebutted.
This motivates self-evolving correction systems that preserve useful
lessons as reusable memory for future claim analysis, evidence
acquisition, and note writing.

## 4 EvoNote: Self-Evolving Health Community Notes Generation

The analysis in
Section [3](#S3 "3 Motivating Analysis: Reusable Misinformation Correction Experience ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")
points to a concrete opportunity: recurring misinformation patterns
expose lessons for later corrections. Motivated by this, EvoNote turns
each correction episode into action-level memory for future note
generation. As shown in
Figure [3](#S3.F3 "Figure 3 ‣ 3.1 Data and Claim Pattern Extraction ‣ 3 Motivating Analysis: Reusable Misinformation Correction Experience ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes"),
a Social Utility Judge grounds trajectory-level feedback in
health-specific note qualities, and a Memory Evolver distills it into
phase-specific strategies for claim analysis, evidence acquisition, and
writing. By learning from its own trajectories, EvoNote adapts to
emerging claims even when reliable human notes are sparse, delayed, or
unavailable. Framework details and a full case are provided in
Appendices [B](#A2 "Appendix B Details of EvoNote Framework ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")
and [I](#A9 "Appendix I Demonstration of EvoNote Workflow ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes").

### 4.1 Note-Generation Episode Formulation

Let $`x_{k}`$ denote the flagged post in episode $`k`$, which may
contain text, image, or video content. We convert $`x_{k}`$ into a
unified textual representation $`\tilde{x}_{k}`$ through captioning,
preserving the multimodal information needed to identify and verify the
health claim. This allows text, image, and video cases to share the same
agentic correction trajectory and supports medical-capable LLMs with
strong tool-use and multi-step reasoning abilities.

A note-generation episode produces a trajectory

|     |     |     |
| --- | --- | --- |
|     |

       ``` math
       \tau_{k}=(\tilde{x}_{k},c_{k},H_{k},E_{k},y_{k}),
       ```                                                |     |

where $`c_{k}`$ is the instance-specific claim analysis, $`H_{k}`$ is
the action history (e.g., “search, visit, …”), $`E_{k}`$ is the
collected evidence, and $`y_{k}`$ is the final generated note. The claim
analysis identifies the core check-worthy claims, priority evidence
needs, and intended correction focus for the current episode.

### 4.2 Trajectory-Level Utility Judgment

At the core of EvoNote is an evolving experience memory that turns
completed correction episodes into actionable guidance. A final note
reveals correction quality, while its trajectory exposes the decisions
behind that quality. EvoNote converts this trajectory-level signal into
structured feedback through a Social Utility Judge agent.

Once the full trajectory $`\tau_{k}`$ for episode $`k`$ is obtained, the
Judge evaluates it and produces fine-grained feedback $`f_{k}`$. The
Judge grounds feedback in a health-correction utility framework drawn
from prior health communication desiderata
(§[B.1](#A2.SS1 "B.1 Trajectory-Level Utility Judgment ‣ Appendix B Details of EvoNote Framework ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")):
(1) understandability for accessible comprehension [Sørensen et al.
(2012)](#bib.bib27); [Warde et al. (2018)](#bib.bib28), (2)
meaningfulness for health interpretation and risk perception [Ferrer and
Klein (2015)](#bib.bib30); [Prike and Ecker (2023)](#bib.bib31), (3)
usability for safe action implications [Heydari et al.
(2021)](#bib.bib29); [Denniss et al. (2022)](#bib.bib26), and (4)
trustworthiness for calibrated evidence use under uncertainty [Schneider
et al. (2021)](#bib.bib23); [Denniss et al. (2022)](#bib.bib26). This
framework captures how a correction becomes useful to the public, moving
from comprehension, to interpretation, to action, to calibrated trust.
The resulting feedback maps note utility back to trajectory decisions,
revealing what the agent should preserve, revise, or avoid in future
claim analysis, evidence acquisition, and writing.

Based on $`f_{k}`$, the judge further assigns a utility mode $`u_{k}`$:
(1) Unsatisfactory, (2) Satisfactory, or (3) Excellent. This mode acts
as a routing signal for memory construction: Unsatisfactory routes the
episode toward failure-avoidance memories, Satisfactory toward
improvement-oriented memories, and Excellent toward success-reuse
memories. Thus, $`f_{k}`$ diagnoses what should be learned from the
trajectory, while $`u_{k}`$ summarizes how the episode should update
memory.

### 4.3 Actionable Memory Evolution

Given the memory-update mode $`u_{k}`$, the key challenge is to make the
completed episode useful beyond the current case. A reusable memory must
specify when it applies, what strategy it recommends, and which
note-generation phase it should guide. The Memory Evolver converts the
completed trajectory into such action-level memory:

|     |                                        |                                                               |     |
| --- | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | --- |
|     | $`\displaystyle\Delta\mathcal{M}^{k}`$ | $`\displaystyle=\textsc{Distill}(\tau_{k},u_{k}),`$           |     |
|     | $`\displaystyle\mathcal{M}^{k}`$       | $`\displaystyle=\mathcal{M}^{k-1}\cup\Delta\mathcal{M}^{k}.`$ |     |

The mode $`u_{k}`$ determines whether the distilled items emphasize
failure avoidance, targeted improvement, or success reuse.

Each memory item in $`\Delta\mathcal{M}^{k}`$ is represented as

|     |     |     |
| --- | --- | --- |
|     |

       ``` math
       m=(\textsc{Trigger},\textsc{ActionStrategy},\textsc{Phase}).
       ```                                                           |     |

Trigger specifies when the memory should be retrieved, ActionStrategy
states the reusable correction strategy, and Phase indicates where it
applies: claim analysis, evidence acquisition, or note writing. This
structure turns episode-level feedback into operational guidance for
future episodes. For example, if a trajectory mishandles a
statistic-based health claim, the Evolver can create an
evidence-acquisition memory that triggers on similar numerical claims
and recommends checking the original source, denominator, and context
before writing.

### 4.4 Memory-Guided Note Generation

At episode $`k+1`$, EvoNote uses the current memory $`\mathcal{M}^{k}`$
to guide a new note-generation trajectory. Given the textual post
representation $`\tilde{x}_{k+1}`$, generation proceeds in two stages:
memory-guided claim analysis, followed by budgeted evidence acquisition
and note writing.

##### Claim Analysis.

The Claim Analyzer agent first summarizes the post into a compact
retrieval query $`q_{C}(\tilde{x}_{k+1})`$ that captures the
correction-relevant claim pattern. It retrieves phase-matched memories
from $`\mathcal{M}^{k}`$ by selecting top-$`n`$ items whose Phase is
claim analysis and whose Trigger has the highest lexical overlap with
the query:

|     |                               |                                                                                  |     |
| --- | ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- |
|     | $`\displaystyle R_{C}^{k+1}`$ | $`\displaystyle=\textsc{Retrieve}\bigl(\mathcal{M}^{k},q_{C}(\tilde{x}_{k+1}),`$ |     |
|     |                               | $`\displaystyle\textsc{Phase}=\textsc{ClaimAnalysis}\bigr).`$                    |     |

The retrieved memories return their ActionStrategy fields, which guide
the analyzer in producing an instance-specific verification brief
$`c_{k+1}`$:

|     |     |     |
| --- | --- | --- |
|     |

       ``` math
       c_{k+1}=C(\tilde{x}_{k+1},R_{C}^{k+1}),
       ```                                      |     |

which specifies the check-worthy claims and priority verification
questions that the subsequent note-generation trajectory should address.

##### Budgeted Evidence Acquisition and Note Writing.

Given $`c_{k+1}`$ and the post representation $`\tilde{x}_{k+1}`$, the
Note Writer agent performs a budgeted action trajectory indexed by step
$`t`$. Before each action step, it summarizes the current decision state
into a retrieval query $`q_{A}^{t}`$, capturing the search history,
collected evidence, remaining uncertainties, and current phase
$`p_{t}`$, where
$`p_{t}\in\{\textsc{EvidenceAcquisition},\textsc{NoteWriting}\}`$. The
writer first uses $`p_{t}`$ to select the phase-matched memory subset,
then retrieves top-$`n`$ memories by lexical overlap between
$`q_{A}^{t}`$ and memory triggers:

|     |                                 |                                                                                                |     |
| --- | ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- |
|     | $`\displaystyle R_{A}^{k+1,t}`$ | $`\displaystyle=\textsc{Retrieve}\bigl(\mathcal{M}^{k},q_{A}^{t},\textsc{Phase}=p_{t}\bigr).`$ |     |

The retrieved ActionStrategy fields guide the next action.

The Writer follows separate budgets for Search and Visit, denoted by
$`B_{S}`$ and $`B_{V}`$. The trajectory starts with evidence-seeking
actions:

|     |     |     |
| --- | --- | --- |
|     |

````math
\mathcal{A}_{t}=\{\textsc{Search},\textsc{Visit}\},\quad a_{t}\in\mathcal{A}_{t}.
``` |  |

Search issues a web query, while Visit inspects either a URL returned by
search or a URL contained in the original post, then extracts
correction-relevant evidence.

After at least one search and one visit, $`\mathcal{A}_{t}`$ expands to
include Write and Abstain:

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathcal{A}_{t}\leftarrow\mathcal{A}_{t}\cup\{\textsc{Write},\textsc{Abstain}\},\quad a_{t}\in\mathcal{A}_{t}.
``` |  |

At all steps, $`\mathcal{A}_{t}`$ is budget-aware: Search is removed
once its search budget $`B_{S}`$ is exhausted, and Visit is removed once
its visit budget $`B_{V}`$ is exhausted. Write drafts a note when
evidence is sufficient and optionally refines it for length compliance;
Abstain terminates generation when evidence cannot support a reliable
correction.

### 4.5 Cross-Episode Self-Evolution

The completed note-generation trajectory of episode $`k+1`$ becomes the
next source of experience. It is evaluated by the Social Utility Judge
and distilled by the Memory Evolver, updating $`\mathcal{M}^{k}`$ into
$`\mathcal{M}^{k+1}`$. Thus, EvoNote forms a closed loop:

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\tau_{k}\rightarrow u_{k}\rightarrow\Delta\mathcal{M}^{k}\rightarrow\tau_{k+1}.
``` |  |

This loop makes correction experience cumulative without updating model
parameters or relying on a fixed bank of human notes, allowing later
episodes to reuse strategies distilled from earlier trajectories.

## 5 The MM-HealthCN Benchmark

We introduce MM-HealthCN, a multimodal benchmark for evaluating health
Community Notes generation under both binary helpfulness judgment and
pairwise social utility comparison.

Data. MM-HealthCN contains 1.2K user-flagged, health-related posts on X,
each paired with a human-written Community Note and its crowd-derived
helpfulness label, either Helpful or Not Helpful. We construct three
modality subsets based on post content: Text, Image, and Video, each
with 400 instances balanced between Helpful and Not Helpful notes.
Details of data construction are provided in
Appendix [C.1](#A3.SS1 "C.1 Source Data Acquisition ‣ Appendix C MM-HealthCN Benchmark Details ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes").

For image and video posts, we use captions as the unified textual input
representation. A pilot test with three independent annotators shows
that captions reliably preserve correction-relevant content, with
majority-vote accuracy of 0.95 on 100 sampled image captions and 0.96 on
100 sampled video captions.
Appendices [C.2](#A3.SS2 "C.2 Multimodal Post Preprocessing ‣ Appendix C MM-HealthCN Benchmark Details ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")
and
[C.3](#A3.SS3 "C.3 Caption Quality Validation ‣ Appendix C MM-HealthCN Benchmark Details ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")
detail the captioning process and validation;
Appendix [F.6](#A6.SS6 "F.6 Captioning Enables More Reliable Agentic Medical Reasoning ‣ Appendix F Additional Results and Analysis ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")
further supports the necessity of captioning by showing the limited
reliability of direct multimodal-VLM instantiation in this agentic
health setting.

Hierarchical Utility Judgment. We extend the hierarchical evaluation
scheme from prior work [Wu et al. (2025)](#bib.bib1), which was
validated with near-perfect human alignment. We first apply a rule-based
platform-compliance filter, marking notes over the 280-character
Community Notes limit as Not Helpful. GPT-4.1-based judges then assess
the remaining notes through three progressive gates: (1) evidence
relevance (R), (2) correctness of evidence representation (C), and (3)
helpfulness of note style (H). A note is deemed Helpful only if it
passes the length filter and all three gates.

To compare notes beyond binary helpfulness, we introduce a GPT-4.1-based
pairwise social utility judge
(§[D.2](#A4.SS2 "D.2 Pairwise Utility Comparison ‣ Appendix D Hierarchical Note Utility Evaluation ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")).
When two notes receive the same binary outcome, the judge performs a
randomized win/tie/loss comparison grounded in four health-specific
utility qualities: understandability, meaningfulness, usability, and
trustworthiness. Human validation with three independent annotators on
100 sampled comparisons shows 98% agreement with the majority vote.
Detailed setup, validation protocols, and judge reliability analyses are
provided in
Appendix [D](#A4 "Appendix D Hierarchical Note Utility Evaluation ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes").

## 6 Experiments

### 6.1 Experimental Setup

Baselines. We compare EvoNote against human-written Community Notes and
three families of automated baselines: (1) web-search-enabled LLMs,
including GPT-4.1 [OpenAI (2025)](#bib.bib8), Grok-4.3 [xAI
(2025)](#bib.bib7), and Gemini-2.5-Flash [Comanici et al.
(2025)](#bib.bib14); (2) LLM-based Community Notes generation systems,
including CrowdNotes+ [Wu et al. (2025)](#bib.bib1) and
DeepResearch-30B-A3B [Tongyi DeepResearch Team et al.
(2025)](#bib.bib16); and (3) memory-augmented LLM agents from Evo-Memory
suite [Wei et al. (2025)](#bib.bib15), including ExpRAG and ReMem. More
details are provided in
Appendix [E.1](#A5.SS1 "E.1 Baselines ‣ Appendix E Experimental Setup ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes").

Implementation Details. EvoNote uses the medical-specific MedGemma-27B
[Sellergren et al. (2025)](#bib.bib6) as the backbone LLM. For fair
comparison, applicable methods share the same web-search interface,
CrowdNotes+, ExpRAG, and ReMem use the same base LLM as EvoNote, and all
memory-based methods retrieve top-$`k`$ memories. Full implementation
details and leakage-control constraints are provided in
Appendices [E.2](#A5.SS2 "E.2 Implementation Details ‣ Appendix E Experimental Setup ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")
and [E.3](#A5.SS3 "E.3 Evaluation Constraints ‣ Appendix E Experimental Setup ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes").

### 6.2 Main Results: Effectiveness of EvoNote

EvoNote improves correction quality both after and before crowd
consensus. On the consensus-resolved MM-HealthCN benchmark, EvoNote
achieves an average 89.6% pairwise win rate over human-written Community
Notes and consistently outperforms all baselines across text, image, and
video posts
(Table [1](#S5.T1 "Table 1 ‣ 5 The MM-HealthCN Benchmark ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")).
The below-50% helpfulness of human-written notes under our hierarchical
judge is consistent with prior findings [Wu et al. (2025)](#bib.bib1)
that crowd-rated helpfulness can mask subtle evidence-related failures,
such as weak source relevance or incorrect evidence representation;
here, we show that this gap extends across modalities. On 300 unresolved
posts whose existing notes remain Needs More Ratings, EvoNote produces
helpful notes in 82.0% of cases, improving coverage before crowd
consensus is reached
(Appendix [F.2](#A6.SS2 "F.2 Applicability to “Needs More Ratings” (NMR) Cases ‣ Appendix F Additional Results and Analysis ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")).

EvoNote rescues failed human notes and strengthens already helpful ones.
For judge-rated Not Helpful human notes in Table
[1](#S5.T1 "Table 1 ‣ 5 The MM-HealthCN Benchmark ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")
($`N=740`$), failures span evidence relevance ($`40.8\%`$), evidence
representation correctness ($`33.2\%`$), and note-style helpfulness
($`25.9\%`$); EvoNote produces a helpful alternative in 77.0% of these
cases. For judge-rated Helpful human notes ($`N=460`$), EvoNote remains
helpful in 87.6% of cases and is preferred in 74.1%.
Figure [4](#S6.F4 "Figure 4 ‣ 6.2 Main Results: Effectiveness of EvoNote ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")
shows gains across all four health-specific utility dimensions,
indicating broader improvements in public-facing correction quality.

Figure 4: Pairwise utility comparison across health-specific utility
dimensions on 403 cases where both human-written notes and EvoNote are
judged Helpful. Ties count as 0.5 for both sides.

Fine-grained evolving memory outperforms generic memory use. Among
MedGemma-27B-based methods, all memory-based agents outperform the
one-pass CrowdNotes+ baseline, confirming the value of reusable
experience. However, EvoNote achieves the strongest performance among
memory-based methods. Unlike ExpRAG, which retrieves full past
trajectories, and ReMem, which asks the actor to infer reusable lessons
from past trajectories, EvoNote explicitly distills judge feedback into
phase-specific memory items for claim analysis, evidence acquisition,
and writing. This highlights the value of phase-directed memory
(§[4.3](#S4.SS3 "4.3 Actionable Memory Evolution ‣ 4 EvoNote: Self-Evolving Health Community Notes Generation ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")):
reusable experience becomes most useful when tied to the correction
stage it should guide.

Both evolving memory and claim analysis matter. We conduct ablations to
isolate self-evolving memory and explicit claim analysis (see details in
Appendix [E.4](#A5.SS4 "E.4 EvoNote Variant Setup ‣ Appendix E Experimental Setup ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")):
EvoNote-fm freezes the warm-up memory bank during evaluation, EvoNote-nm
removes memory retrieval and update, and EvoNote-nm-na further removes
the Claim Analyzer.
Table [1](#S5.T1 "Table 1 ‣ 5 The MM-HealthCN Benchmark ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")
shows that each removal degrades performance, confirming that EvoNote
benefits from both accumulated experience and instance-specific
verification planning.

## 7 Discussion

EvoNote uses stronger and more diverse evidence. We compare EvoNote with
representative baselines using five evidence-side metrics: average cited
URLs, multi-URL rate, source quality, cited-domain diversity, and
semantic diversity (detailed in
Appendix [F.3](#A6.SS3 "F.3 Evidence Use Analysis ‣ Appendix F Additional Results and Analysis ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")).
These metrics measure cross-source support, source credibility, and
evidence diversity.
Figure [5](#S7.F5 "Figure 5 ‣ 7 Discussion ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")
shows that EvoNote achieves the strongest overall evidence profile, with
more multi-source support, higher source quality, and stronger domain
and semantic diversity. This suggests that self-evolving memory guides
more deliberate evidence acquisition for later episodes.

Figure 5: Evidence quality and diversity of EvoNote compared with
representative baselines. Metrics are defined in
Appendix [F.3](#A6.SS3 "F.3 Evidence Use Analysis ‣ Appendix F Additional Results and Analysis ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes").

EvoNote improves quality with moderate cost. As shown in
Table [2](#S7.T2 "Table 2 ‣ 7 Discussion ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes"),
EvoNote achieves the highest win rate while using fewer turns and less
total time than DeepResearch and ReMem. This suggests that
phase-specific memory improves the quality-efficiency trade-off: EvoNote
avoids the heavier information seeking of DeepResearch and the
full-trajectory reasoning cost of ReMem by retrieving compact
action-level strategies at the relevant correction stage.

| Model        | $`\overline{T}`$ | Search | Visit | Infer. | Total | Win.  |
|--------------|------------------|--------|-------|--------|-------|-------|
| CrowdNotes+  | 6.0              | 4.8    | 23.5  | 17.9   | 46.2  | 69.21 |
| DeepResearch | 13.7             | 12.8   | 71.3  | 68.9   | 153.0 | 78.09 |
| ExpRAG       | 8.6              | 6.1    | 34.7  | 30.2   | 71.0  | 79.63 |
| ReMem        | 15.6             | 5.4    | 47.6  | 65.3   | 118.3 | 74.50 |
| EvoNote      | 12.4             | 7.9    | 55.1  | 49.6   | 112.6 | 89.59 |

Table 2: Time efficiency on MM-HealthCN using a single H200 GPU. We
report mean turns $`\overline{T}`$, mean time (s) for search, visit,
inference (note generation), mean total time, and Win rate over
human-written notes.

EvoNote learns actionable health misinformation correction strategies.
Across MM-HealthCN, EvoNote accumulates 4,277 memory items, each tied to
an action phase and reusable strategy. Using a human-built attribution
taxonomy and GPT-4.1 classification, we find that the dominant memories
target primary-source verification, causal overgeneralization, safe next
steps, and practical health implications (see
§[F.4](#A6.SS4 "F.4 Memory Utility Analysis ‣ Appendix F Additional Results and Analysis ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")).
These phase-specific strategies address recurring correction failures.
Figure [11](#A6.F11 "Figure 11 ‣ F.5 Case Study: Retrieved Memory Guides Regulatory-Process Verification ‣ Appendix F Additional Results and Analysis ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")
and
§[F.5](#A6.SS5 "F.5 Case Study: Retrieved Memory Guides Regulatory-Process Verification ‣ Appendix F Additional Results and Analysis ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")
further show one memory-guided case where retrieved experience improves
evidence seeking and note framing over human notes, Grok-4.3,
CrowdNotes+, and ReMem.

Captioning enables more reliable agentic health-related reasoning. We
examine whether EvoNote should directly instantiate its trajectory with
a multimodal medical VLM. On the Image subset, EvoNote with a multimodal
MedGemma-27B backbone fails to complete valid note-generation
trajectories in nearly all cases; even after complex repair heuristics,
63 cases remain invalid (see
Appendix [F.6](#A6.SS6 "F.6 Captioning Enables More Reliable Agentic Medical Reasoning ‣ Appendix F Additional Results and Analysis ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")).
On this basis,
Figure [6](#S7.F6 "Figure 6 ‣ 7 Discussion ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")
shows that the VLM version still underperforms the caption-based LLM
pipeline, even below the no-memory LLM variant. This supports our
captioning design: human-validated captions preserve correction-relevant
visual content, while medical-capable LLMs offer more reliable tool use,
evidence acquisition, and multi-step reasoning.

Figure 6: VLM and caption-based LLM instantiations of EvoNote on 400
Image cases.

## 8 Conclusion

We presented EvoNote, a self-evolving agentic approach to health
Community Notes generation. Our findings show that misinformation
correction can become cumulative: recurring claims expose reusable
correction experience, and agentic systems can improve by carrying that
experience forward. On MM-HealthCN, EvoNote outperforms human-written
notes and strong automated baselines, with gains supported by stronger
evidence use and actionable memory. This points to a broader design
principle for misinformation governance, where each agentic correction
trajectory should leave behind reusable experience for addressing the
next similar claim.

## Limitations

This work shows that health misinformation correction can become
cumulative by turning agentic correction trajectories into reusable
memory. Several extensions remain open.

First, EvoNote focuses on English health misinformation. This setting is
high-stakes and evidence-centric, making it suitable for studying
reusable correction experience. Extending to political, financial, or
sociocultural claims may require different utility criteria, as evidence
can be more contested and context-dependent. Multilingual deployment
also raises challenges in source coverage, local authority
representation, and culturally grounded risk communication.

Second, EvoNote learns mainly from its own trajectories. Human-written
notes are used for benchmarking and motivating analysis, while memory is
distilled from agent-generated correction episodes. Future work could
jointly learn from agent trajectories and high-quality human
corrections. This may improve memory quality, but requires careful
filtering because crowd-sourced signals can be noisy, incomplete, or
affected by voting dynamics.

Third, self-evolution is implemented at the memory level. The backbone
model, tools, and workflow remain fixed; adaptation comes from
accumulating phase-specific action memories. This makes improvement
interpretable and lightweight, but leaves broader forms of
self-evolution, such as prompt revision, workflow adaptation, and
tool-policy learning, for future work.

Finally, EvoNote starts from flagged posts. We do not model upstream
detection, prioritization, or real-time routing. Practical deployment
should integrate self-evolving note generation with systems that
identify emerging misinformation, estimate urgency, and decide when
human review is needed.

## Ethical Considerations

##### Human Oversight in Health Correction.

Health corrections can affect public understanding, risk perception, and
health-related decisions. EvoNote should therefore be used as a
human-augmenting system, not an autonomous arbiter of truth. Human
reviewers should inspect cited evidence, verify medical claims, and
decide whether a generated note is appropriate to surface.

##### Over-Trust and Automation Bias.

Generated notes may appear authoritative even when evidence is
incomplete or misrepresented. This risk is especially important in
health contexts, where fluent explanations can hide subtle errors.
Interfaces built around EvoNote should encourage active verification by
exposing evidence snippets, highlighting uncertainty, and requiring
source inspection before approval.

##### Memory Safety.

Self-evolving memory makes correction experience cumulative, which is a
core strength of EvoNote. It can also propagate flawed lessons if
incorrect trajectories are stored. Future deployments should include
memory auditing, revision, decay, and deletion mechanisms to prevent
outdated or incorrect strategies from persisting.

##### Dual Use and Selective Evidence Use.

Evidence-grounded note generation could be misused to produce persuasive
but misleading corrections, cherry-pick sources, or suppress legitimate
scientific disagreement. Mitigations should include transparent evidence
presentation, source-diversity auditing, and safeguards against
selective or adversarial use.

##### Data Use and Privacy.

Our study uses public Community Notes data, public posts, and publicly
accessible web evidence, without relying on private user information.
Released benchmark resources should follow platform policies and be
shared under research-oriented access conditions to support
reproducibility while reducing privacy and misuse risks.

## Appendix A Details of Motivating Analysis

This appendix provides details for the motivating analysis in
§[3](#S3 "3 Motivating Analysis: Reusable Misinformation Correction Experience ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes"):
including data filtering
(§[A.1](#A1.SS1 "A.1 Health-Related Data Filtering ‣ Appendix A Details of Motivating Analysis ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")),
claim pattern extraction
(§[A.2](#A1.SS2 "A.2 Claim Pattern Extraction ‣ Appendix A Details of Motivating Analysis ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")),
and additional latency/visibility statistics
(§[A.3](#A1.SS3 "A.3 Latency and Visibility Statistics ‣ Appendix A Details of Motivating Analysis ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")).

### A.1 Health-Related Data Filtering

We collect publicly available, user-contributed Community Notes on X²² 2
[https://x.com/i/communitynotes/download-data](https://x.com/i/communitynotes/download-data)
up to 14 October 2025 and retain English entries for consistency.

To identify health-related notes, we follow the extraction pipeline of
[Wu et al. (2025)](#bib.bib1), which defines seven health-topic
categories and validates a zero-shot filtering approach with Lingshu-32B
[Xu et al. (2025)](#bib.bib5), a medical LLM. We adopt the same
categories: (1) diseases or medical conditions, (2) drugs, vaccines,
treatments, and tests, (3) public health guidance or policy, (4)
wellness products, diets, and supplements, (5) healthcare professionals
or systems, (6) biological or epidemiological concepts, and (7)
health-related conspiracies or hoaxes.

We use the following prompt for Lingshu-32B:

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

We then retrieve the associated flagged posts from X and remove
unavailable posts or URL-only content. This yields 48,295 notes
addressing 40,116 health-related flagged posts. Among them, 6,336 notes
(13.12%) have crowd-derived helpfulness labels, including 4,874
“Helpful” notes and 1,462 “Not Helpful” notes. The remaining cases are
unresolved, i.e., “Needs More Ratings”.

### A.2 Claim Pattern Extraction

We detail the correction-relevant claim taxonomy used in
§[3.1](#S3.SS1 "3.1 Data and Claim Pattern Extraction ‣ 3 Motivating Analysis: Reusable Misinformation Correction Experience ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes").
We derive claim patterns from the 4,874 Helpful human-written notes
obtained in
§[A.1](#A1.SS1 "A.1 Health-Related Data Filtering ‣ Appendix A Details of Motivating Analysis ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes"),
using them as high-precision signals for what made a flagged health post
misleading and what evidence or framing made the correction useful.

Starting from recurring health misinformation patterns reported in prior
work [Wang et al. (2019)](#bib.bib34); [Kington et al.
(2021)](#bib.bib24); [Ngai et al. (2022)](#bib.bib33); [Watson et al.
(2024)](#bib.bib32), two human experts reviewed 200 sampled post-note
pairs, summarized the main misleading mechanisms, and merged overlapping
labels into the compact taxonomy in
Table [4](#A1.T4 "Table 4 ‣ A.3 Latency and Visibility Statistics ‣ Appendix A Details of Motivating Analysis ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes").
Each category captures a recurring misleading mechanism, while its
description notes the typical correction need revealed by helpful notes.

We then use GPT-4.1 [OpenAI (2025)](#bib.bib8) to classify the remaining
helpful-note cases under this taxonomy. For posts involving multiple
mechanisms, we assign the primary pattern according to the correction
strategy most central to the helpful note. The resulting distribution,
reported in
Figure [2](#S2.F2 "Figure 2 ‣ 2 Related Work ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes"),
supports our analysis of recurring correction needs.

| Post Modality | Post-to-Note | Note-to-Verdict |
|---------------|--------------|-----------------|
| Text          | 6.3          | 7.3             |
| Text & Image  | 7.1          | 6.6             |
| Text & Video  | 6.1          | 6.4             |

Table 3: Median latency (in hours) for health Community Notes across
post modalities. Post-to-Note measures time from post creation to first
note; Note-to-Verdict measures time from note creation to crowd-derived
helpfulness verdict.

### A.3 Latency and Visibility Statistics

We provide contextual statistics on the timeliness and coverage
challenges of health Community Notes for correcting multimodal
misleading posts, complementing the motivating analysis in
§[3](#S3 "3 Motivating Analysis: Reusable Misinformation Correction Experience ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes").
We compute two latency metrics: (1) post-to-note latency, the time from
post creation to the first note, and (2) note-to-verdict latency, the
time from note creation to a crowd-derived helpfulness verdict, i.e.,
Helpful or Not Helpful. We also measure verdict coverage, the percentage
of notes that receive such a verdict.

We compute latency over the 6,336 health-related notes with
crowd-derived helpfulness verdicts (obtained in
§[A.1](#A1.SS1 "A.1 Health-Related Data Filtering ‣ Appendix A Details of Motivating Analysis ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")).
As shown in
Table [3](#A1.T3 "Table 3 ‣ A.2 Claim Pattern Extraction ‣ Appendix A Details of Motivating Analysis ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes"),
median post-to-note latency is 6.1–7.1 hours across modalities, while
median note-to-verdict latency is 6.4–7.3 hours. This means a misleading
health post typically takes over 13 hours to receive a resolved
Community Note, indicating a substantial delay for time-sensitive health
correction.

Note coverage is also limited. Among all 48,295 health-related notes,
only 6,336 notes (13.12%) receive a crowd-derived verdict, including
2,624 text-only cases, 2,207 text-image cases, and 1,505 text-video
cases. The remaining 86.88% stay unresolved as Needs More Ratings.
Moreover, only 4,874 notes, 10.1% of all health-related notes, are
ultimately rated Helpful. These results show that many correction
efforts remain delayed, unresolved, or never become visible as helpful
corrections, echoing prior findings on Community Notes latency and
coverage [Renault et al. (2024)](#bib.bib13); [Wu et al.
(2025)](#bib.bib1). This motivates LLM-augmented note generation
approaches that can create evidence-grounded notes earlier while crowd
consensus is still forming.

[TABLE]

Table 4: Correction-relevant health misinformation patterns. Two human
annotators construct these categories from 200 sampled helpful-note
cases; descriptions summarize the misleading mechanism and the
