````math
## Appendix B Details of EvoNote Framework

This appendix details the main components of the EvoNote framework
described in
§[4](#S4 "4 EvoNote: Self-Evolving Health Community Notes Generation ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes").
The detailed prompts are given in
§[H](#A8 "Appendix H Prompts for EvoNote ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes"),
and a complete trajectory example is provided in
§[I](#A9 "Appendix I Demonstration of EvoNote Workflow ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes").

### B.1 Trajectory-Level Utility Judgment

The Social Utility Judge agent implements the credit-assignment role
introduced in
§[4.2](#S4.SS2 "4.2 Trajectory-Level Utility Judgment ‣ 4 EvoNote: Self-Evolving Health Community Notes Generation ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes").
Its role is to convert a completed note-generation trajectory into
diagnostic feedback for future learning. Given the full trajectory,
including claim analysis, search and visit actions, collected evidence,
and the generated note, the Judge evaluates how the trajectory supports
or weakens the final correction.

The Judge grounds this evaluation in four health-specific note qualities
drawn from prior work in health communication. Understandability
explains key distinctions or jargon in accessible language, helping
readers grasp the correction without medical expertise [Sørensen et al.
(2012)](#bib.bib27); [Warde et al. (2018)](#bib.bib28); [Denniss et al.
(2022)](#bib.bib26). Meaningfulness clarifies why the correction matters
for health interpretation, risk perception, or behavior, making its
practical significance explicit [Ferrer and Klein (2015)](#bib.bib30);
[Heydari et al. (2021)](#bib.bib29); [Prike and Ecker
(2023)](#bib.bib31). Usability provides safe and proportionate next-step
guidance when user action may be affected, supporting responsible public
decision-making [Denniss et al. (2022)](#bib.bib26); [Heydari et al.
(2021)](#bib.bib29). Trustworthiness avoids overclaiming and
acknowledges uncertainty or evidence limits where appropriate,
preserving reliability under evolving medical evidence [Denniss et al.
(2022)](#bib.bib26); [Schneider et al. (2021)](#bib.bib23); [Kington et
al. (2021)](#bib.bib24). These qualities define whether a correction is
accessible to readers, useful for health interpretation, actionable when
user behavior may be affected, and calibrated under evidence
uncertainty. The full Judge prompt is provided in
Figure [12](#A8.F12 "Figure 12 ‣ Appendix H Prompts for EvoNote ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes").

The Judge produces two outputs. First, it provides fine-grained feedback
that attributes note utility to trajectory decisions, such as claim
analysis, evidence acquisition, uncertainty handling, or writing.
Second, it assigns an overall utility mode, Unsatisfactory,
Satisfactory, or Excellent, which determines how the trajectory should
be converted into memory. This turns final-note evaluation into a
structured learning signal for the Memory Evolver.

### B.2 Actionable Memory Evolution

The Memory Evolver agent implements the memory-construction role
introduced in
§[4.3](#S4.SS3 "4.3 Actionable Memory Evolution ‣ 4 EvoNote: Self-Evolving Health Community Notes Generation ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes").
Its role is to transform the Judge’s feedback into reusable action-level
memories. This step is necessary because raw trajectories contain many
instance-specific details, such as URLs, query paths, and post-specific
wording, that cannot be directly reused in future cases.

Given the trajectory and Judge outputs, the Evolver abstracts the
episode into compact correction strategies. The full Memory Evolver
prompt is provided in
Figure [13](#A8.F13 "Figure 13 ‣ Appendix H Prompts for EvoNote ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes").
Each generated memory item follows the schema

|     |                                                              |     |
|-----|--------------------------------------------------------------|-----|
|     |
       ``` math
       m=(\textsc{Trigger},\textsc{ActionStrategy},\textsc{Phase}).
       ```                                                           |     |

Trigger specifies when the memory should be retrieved, ActionStrategy
states the reusable correction lesson, and Phase assigns the lesson to
claim analysis, evidence acquisition, or note writing.

This structure makes memory directly actionable. Instead of storing full
trajectories or generic reflections, EvoNote stores phase-specific
guidance that can be retrieved at the point where it is useful. For
example, a failed trajectory on a statistic-based health claim may yield
an evidence-acquisition memory that triggers on similar numerical claims
and recommends checking the original source, denominator, and
surrounding context before writing.

### B.3 Memory-Guided Note Generation

Memory-guided generation implements the inference-time process
introduced in
§[4.4](#S4.SS4 "4.4 Memory-Guided Note Generation ‣ 4 EvoNote: Self-Evolving Health Community Notes Generation ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes").
Its role is to use the current memory bank to guide a new
note-generation episode without updating model parameters. The process
is implemented through two prompt-driven agents: a Claim Analyzer agent
and a Note Writer agent.

At each stage, EvoNote retrieves memories whose triggers match the
current post or decision state and whose phase matches the current
generation stage. The retrieved ActionStrategy fields guide the next
step, while the final note remains grounded in evidence collected during
the current episode. This allows prior experience to shape the
trajectory while preserving instance-specific evidence verification.

#### B.3.1 Claim Analyzer

The Claim Analyzer performs the first memory-guided stage of note
generation. Its role is to turn the flagged post into a focused
verification brief before evidence acquisition begins. Given the post
representation and retrieved claim-analysis memories, the Claim Analyzer
identifies the central check-worthy claims, priority verification
questions, and evidence needs.

The Claim Analyzer prompt is provided in
Figure [14](#A8.F14 "Figure 14 ‣ Appendix H Prompts for EvoNote ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes").
Its output follows a structured verification-brief schema, including the
likely claim pattern, check-worthy claims, priority questions, evidence
needs, correction focus, and relevant memory guidance. This brief
defines what the Note Writer should verify and what kind of evidence it
should seek.

The effect is to make evidence acquisition less reactive and more
targeted. Instead of beginning from surface wording alone, the Note
Writer starts from a memory-informed account of what must be checked,
why it matters, and which recurring correction strategies may apply.

#### B.3.2 Note Writer

The Note Writer executes the memory-guided correction trajectory. Its
role is to acquire evidence and generate the final Community Note based
on the verification brief, the current action history, collected
evidence, and retrieved phase-matched memories.

At each step, the Note Writer selects one action from the available
action space. It may issue a Search query, Visit a source returned by
search or contained in the original post, Write a note when evidence is
sufficient, or Abstain when the available evidence cannot support a
reliable correction. The Note Writer prompt is provided in
Figure [15](#A8.F15 "Figure 15 ‣ Appendix H Prompts for EvoNote ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes").
Retrieved memories guide query formulation, source prioritization,
stopping decisions, uncertainty calibration, and note framing, but they
are never treated as evidence themselves.

This design lets EvoNote reuse prior correction experience while
maintaining evidence grounding for each new post. The resulting
trajectory records the actions taken, the evidence collected, and the
final note, which then becomes the next source of experience for the
Social Utility Judge and Memory Evolver.

## Appendix C MM-HealthCN Benchmark Details

### C.1 Source Data Acquisition

We construct MM-HealthCN by sampling 1,200 instances from the 6,336
health-related post–note pairs with crowd-derived verdicts obtained in
§[A.1](#A1.SS1 "A.1 Health-Related Data Filtering ‣ Appendix A Details of Motivating Analysis ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes").
To support controlled evaluation across modalities and note quality, we
create three modality subsets, Text, Image, and Video, each containing
400 instances balanced between Helpful and Not Helpful human-written
notes. This balanced design enables evaluation both on cases where
existing human notes are useful and on cases where automated systems may
provide better alternatives.

Figure [7](#A3.F7 "Figure 7 ‣ C.1 Source Data Acquisition ‣ Appendix C MM-HealthCN Benchmark Details ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")
shows the topic distribution of MM-HealthCN. Following prior work [Wu et
al. (2025)](#bib.bib1), we assign each instance to one health topic
(§[A.1](#A1.SS1 "A.1 Health-Related Data Filtering ‣ Appendix A Details of Motivating Analysis ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes"))
using GPT-4.1 with temperature 0, based on the post text and, for image
or video posts, the captioned multimodal content described in
§[C.2](#A3.SS2 "C.2 Multimodal Post Preprocessing ‣ Appendix C MM-HealthCN Benchmark Details ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes").
Across modalities, the benchmark covers diverse health misinformation
topics, with drugs, vaccines, treatments, and medical conditions forming
the largest shares, while video posts contain a higher proportion of
conspiracy or hoax-related content. This distribution reflects the
heterogeneous correction challenges faced by multimodal health Community
Notes.

![Refer to caption](2606.02215v1/dataset-stats.png)

Figure 7: Topic distribution of MM-HealthCN. Instances are grouped by
post modality and assigned to representative health topics following
prior work [Wu et al. (2025)](#bib.bib1).

![Refer to caption](2606.02215v1/human-instruction-caption.png)

Figure 8: Human validation protocol for multimodal caption quality
(§[C.2](#A3.SS2 "C.2 Multimodal Post Preprocessing ‣ Appendix C MM-HealthCN Benchmark Details ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")).

### C.2 Multimodal Post Preprocessing

We convert multimodal posts into textual representations so that image
and video cases can share the same agentic note-generation pipeline as
text-only cases. This design preserves the tool-use and multi-step
reasoning strengths of LLM backbones while retaining correction-relevant
visual information through captions.
§[F.6](#A6.SS6 "F.6 Captioning Enables More Reliable Agentic Medical Reasoning ‣ Appendix F Additional Results and Analysis ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")
further analyzes why direct multimodal-VLM instantiation is less
reliable in this setting.

For image posts, we use Nanonets Docstrange³³ 3
[https://github.com/NanoNets/docstrange](https://github.com/NanoNets/docstrange).,
which is designed for faithful extraction of visual and textual content
from images. For video posts, we use Gemini-2.5-Flash [Comanici et al.
(2025)](#bib.bib14) to summarize correction-relevant visual content,
on-screen text, and temporal context. The resulting captions are
concatenated with the original post text as the unified input
representation.

### C.3 Caption Quality Validation

To verify that captioning preserves correction-relevant content, we
conduct a human validation study on 200 randomly sampled multimodal
instances from MM-HealthCN, including 100 Image and 100 Video cases. As
shown in
Figure [8](#A3.F8 "Figure 8 ‣ C.1 Source Data Acquisition ‣ Appendix C MM-HealthCN Benchmark Details ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes"),
annotators view the original post and generated caption side by side,
and judge whether the caption accurately reflects the multimodal content
needed for verifying the post.

Three annotators independently label each instance. For image captions,
majority-vote accuracy is 0.95; for video captions, it is 0.96. Only 5
out of 100 cases show annotator disagreement in each setting. These
results indicate that caption-based representations reliably preserve
the information needed for multimodal health misinformation correction.

## Appendix D Hierarchical Note Utility Evaluation

This appendix details the hierarchical note utility evaluation scheme of
MM-HealthCN
(§[5](#S5 "5 The MM-HealthCN Benchmark ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")).

Our evaluation proceeds in two stages. First, building on the
human-validated helpfulness judgment protocol of [Wu et al.
(2025)](#bib.bib1), we determine whether a note is Helpful through
length compliance and progressive checks of evidence relevance, evidence
correctness, and note-style helpfulness
(§[D.1](#A4.SS1 "D.1 Hierarchical Helpfulness Judgment ‣ Appendix D Hierarchical Note Utility Evaluation ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")).
Second, for notes with the same binary helpfulness outcome, we compare
their public-facing social utility through randomized pairwise judgment
(§[D.2](#A4.SS2 "D.2 Pairwise Utility Comparison ‣ Appendix D Hierarchical Note Utility Evaluation ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")).

### D.1 Hierarchical Helpfulness Judgment

A note is deemed Helpful only if it passes the following four gates in a
progressive order.

Gate 1: Length Compliance. Community Notes must not exceed 280
characters, with each URL counted as one character⁴⁴ 4
[https://docs.x.com/x-api/community-notes/quickstart](https://docs.x.com/x-api/community-notes/quickstart);
notes exceeding this are labeled Not Helpful by a rule-based filter.

Gate 2: Evidence Relevance. The cited evidence must provide factual
context or clarification that helps readers evaluate the claim in the
post.

Gate 3: Evidence Representation Correctness. The note must accurately
represent the cited sources without factual errors, exaggeration, or
misleading framing, addressing a common risk in scientific and medical
communication [Glockner et al. (2024)](#bib.bib39); [Wührl et al.
(2024)](#bib.bib40).

Gate 4: Note-Style Helpfulness. Following Community Notes guidelines,
the note must provide useful context that helps readers understand or
critically evaluate the flagged post.

##### Gate Implementation.

Gate 1 is implemented with the rule-based length filter above. For Gates
2 and 3, we use the GPT-4.1-based prompts from the helpfulness judgment
protocol of [Wu et al. (2025)](#bib.bib1). For Gate 4, we use
HealthJudge, a Lingshu-7B-based binary helpfulness classifier fine-tuned
on health Community Note post–note pairs by [Wu et al.
(2025)](#bib.bib1). Since the Gates 2–4 judges are adopted without
modification, we refer readers to [Wu et al. (2025)](#bib.bib1) for full
prompt details. Failure at any gate labels the note as Not Helpful.
Judge reliability results are provided in
§[D.3.1](#A4.SS3.SSS1 "D.3.1 Reliability of Hierarchical Helpfulness Judgment ‣ D.3 Reliability of LLM Judges ‣ Appendix D Hierarchical Note Utility Evaluation ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes").

### D.2 Pairwise Utility Comparison

Binary helpfulness indicates whether a note meets a minimum quality bar,
but it does not distinguish between two notes that are both helpful or
both unhelpful. We therefore add pairwise utility comparison to capture
which note better serves public-facing health correction.

Given two candidate notes, a GPT4.1-based judge compares them in
randomized order and first reasons over fine-grained
health-communication criteria. It then assigns a final outcome, win,
lose, or tie, based on the overall social utility of the two notes. The
criteria are grounded in established desiderata for health
communication: (1) understandability, explaining key distinctions or
necessary jargon in accessible language [Sørensen et al.
(2012)](#bib.bib27); [Warde et al. (2018)](#bib.bib28); [Denniss et al.
(2022)](#bib.bib26); (2) meaningfulness, clarifying why the correction
matters for health interpretation, risk perception, or behavior [Ferrer
and Klein (2015)](#bib.bib30); [Heydari et al. (2021)](#bib.bib29);
[Prike and Ecker (2023)](#bib.bib31); (3) usability, providing safe and
proportionate next steps when the claim may affect user action [Denniss
et al. (2022)](#bib.bib26); [Heydari et al. (2021)](#bib.bib29); and (4)
trustworthiness, avoiding overclaiming and acknowledging uncertainty or
evidence limits where appropriate [Denniss et al. (2022)](#bib.bib26);
[Schneider et al. (2021)](#bib.bib23); [Kington et al.
(2021)](#bib.bib24).

Figure [9](#A4.F9 "Figure 9 ‣ D.2 Pairwise Utility Comparison ‣ Appendix D Hierarchical Note Utility Evaluation ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")
shows the prompt used for pairwise utility comparison. We provide
results on judge reliability in
§[D.3.2](#A4.SS3.SSS2 "D.3.2 Reliability of Pairwise Utility Comparison ‣ D.3 Reliability of LLM Judges ‣ Appendix D Hierarchical Note Utility Evaluation ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes").

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Figure 9: Prompt for pairwise utility judgment between two Community
Notes candidates.

### D.3 Reliability of LLM Judges

To ensure reliable evaluation, we validate the LLM-based components used
in hierarchical helpfulness judgment and pairwise utility comparison
against human-aligned tests.

#### D.3.1 Reliability of Hierarchical Helpfulness Judgment

Length compliance is checked by a rule-based filter that directly
follows the platform-enforced 280-character constraint. For evidence
relevance and evidence representation correctness, we use the
GPT-4.1-based judges from [Wu et al. (2025)](#bib.bib1), which were
shown to achieve near-perfect human alignment on health Community Note
evaluation.

We further test whether HealthJudge, the Gate 4 helpfulness classifier,
generalizes to our multimodal setting. We randomly sample 1,000
post-note pairs covering Text, Image, and Video cases, and compare
HealthJudge with strong proprietary LLM judges, including GPT-4.1 and
Claude-Sonnet-4. As shown in
Table [5](#A4.T5 "Table 5 ‣ D.3.1 Reliability of Hierarchical Helpfulness Judgment ‣ D.3 Reliability of LLM Judges ‣ Appendix D Hierarchical Note Utility Evaluation ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes"),
HealthJudge achieves the strongest performance, supporting its use as
the final helpfulness gate after evidence relevance (Gate 2) and
correctness (Gate 3) have been verified.

We refer readers to [Wu et al. (2025)](#bib.bib1) for the original human
evaluation setup, prompt details, and HealthJudge training procedure.

| Model            | Macro-F1 (%) | Macro-Acc. (%) |
|------------------|--------------|----------------|
| GPT-4.1          | 74.30        | 71.67          |
| Gemini-2.5-flash | 67.86        | 64.35          |
| Claude-Sonnet-4  | 74.58        | 72.40          |
| HealthJudge      | 89.21        | 88.46          |

Table 5: Effectiveness of HealthJudge for note helpfulness assessment,
validated by its superior performance on 1,000 unseen pairs of
multimodal posts and corresponding notes (see
§[D.3.1](#A4.SS3.SSS1 "D.3.1 Reliability of Hierarchical Helpfulness Judgment ‣ D.3 Reliability of LLM Judges ‣ Appendix D Hierarchical Note Utility Evaluation ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")).

#### D.3.2 Reliability of Pairwise Utility Comparison

To validate the GPT-4.1-based pairwise utility judge, we conduct a human
alignment study on 100 randomly sampled note pairs. For each pair, three
annotators independently review the flagged post, the two candidate
notes, and the judge’s dimension-level decisions and rationales,
following the instruction in
Figure [10](#A4.F10 "Figure 10 ‣ D.3.2 Reliability of Pairwise Utility Comparison ‣ D.3 Reliability of LLM Judges ‣ Appendix D Hierarchical Note Utility Evaluation ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes").
Annotators decide whether the judge’s comparison is accurate.

The pairwise judge agrees with the human majority vote in 98% of cases.
Only 4 out of 100 cases show inter-annotator disagreement, indicating
strong annotator consistency. These results support the reliability of
using the pairwise judge to compare public-facing social utility beyond
binary helpfulness.

Figure 10: Human evaluation instruction for validating GPT-4.1-based
pairwise utility judgments
(§[D.2](#A4.SS2 "D.2 Pairwise Utility Comparison ‣ Appendix D Hierarchical Note Utility Evaluation ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")).

## Appendix E Experimental Setup

This appendix supplements the experimental setup in
§[6.1](#S6.SS1 "6.1 Experimental Setup ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")
with details on baseline implementation
(§[E.1](#A5.SS1 "E.1 Baselines ‣ Appendix E Experimental Setup ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")),
shared implementation settings
(§[E.2](#A5.SS2 "E.2 Implementation Details ‣ Appendix E Experimental Setup ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")),
necessary evaluation constraints for fair comparison
(§[E.3](#A5.SS3 "E.3 Evaluation Constraints ‣ Appendix E Experimental Setup ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")),
and EvoNote variants used for controlled comparisons
(§[E.4](#A5.SS4 "E.4 EvoNote Variant Setup ‣ Appendix E Experimental Setup ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")).

### E.1 Baselines

We compare EvoNote with three groups of baselines that cover
progressively stronger forms of automated note generation.

##### Web-search-enabled LLMs.

These baselines test whether strong general-purpose LLMs with external
search can generate helpful notes without task-specific Community Notes
design or memory:

- •
  GPT-4.1 [OpenAI (2025)](#bib.bib8),
- •
  Grok-4.3 [xAI (2025)](#bib.bib7),
- •
  Gemini-2.5-Flash [Comanici et al. (2025)](#bib.bib14).

##### LLM-based Community Notes generation systems.

These baselines represent task-adapted note-generation pipelines that
explicitly target Community Notes-style correction:

- •
  CrowdNotes+ [Wu et al. (2025)](#bib.bib1), based on MedGemma-27B
  [Sellergren et al. (2025)](#bib.bib6) and instantiated under its Note
  Automation mode for automated evidence exploration; the evidence
  budget (top-$`k`$ evidence retrieved) is aligned with the number of
  evidences retrieved by EvoNote for a fair comparison.
- •
  DeepResearch [Tongyi DeepResearch Team et al. (2025)](#bib.bib16), a
  30B open-source agent adapted as a search-intensive note-generation
  agent.

##### Memory-augmented LLM agents.

These baselines test whether generic agent memory mechanisms can support
reusable correction experience without the phase-specific memory design
of EvoNote:

- •
  ExpRAG, which retrieves prior trajectories as task-level context;
- •
  ReMem, which integrates reasoning, action, and memory refinement for
  continual improvement.

Both are adapted from the Evo-Memory suite [Wei et al.
(2025)](#bib.bib15).

### E.2 Implementation Details

##### LLM Setup.

For web-search-enabled LLM baselines, we evaluate GPT-4.1, Grok-4.3, and
Gemini-2.5-Flash through the OpenRouter API⁵⁵ 5
[https://openrouter.ai/](https://openrouter.ai/), using each model’s
official web-search capability when available. We set temperature=0.0,
top_p=1.0, and max_tokens=1024, and disable reasoning mode for Grok-4.3
and Gemini-2.5-Flash.

For LLM-based Community Notes generation systems, CrowdNotes+ follows
the original implementation. DeepResearch uses
Alibaba-NLP/Tongyi-DeepResearch-30B-A3B following its official technical
report, with temperature=0.85, repetition penalty 1.1, top_p=0.95, up to
128 tool calls, and the unchanged official prompt.

For memory-augmented agents, ExpRAG, ReMem, and EvoNote use
google/medgemma-27b-text-it as the backbone LLM, deployed with vLLM on a
single H200 GPU, with temperature=0.0 for all calls for stability.

All experiments are run once.

##### Agent Configuration.

For ExpRAG, ReMem, and EvoNote, we use the same execution budget: at
most 15 steps, 5 searches, and 12 page visits. Each episode requires at
least one search and one visit before finalization, allows up to 5
write-refinement attempts, and is rerun up to 5 times upon execution
failure. Memory retrieval selects top-$`k`$ entries by lexical overlap
with $`k=4`$. We process the dataset with batch size 4 for memory
updates. For ReMem, we set the maximum memory-refinement loop to 4.

##### Search and Visit API Use.

We use Serper⁶⁶ 6 [https://serper.dev/](https://serper.dev/) for search
and Firecrawl⁷⁷ 7
[https://www.firecrawl.dev/](https://www.firecrawl.dev/) for page
visiting. Search returns up to 10 time-constrained results, deduplicates
canonical URLs, and falls back to answer-box links when available. Visit
extracts main-page markdown, retries failed or CAPTCHA-like pages with
backoff and stealth proxy, and optionally falls back to Jina Reader⁸⁸ 8
[https://jina.ai/](https://jina.ai/). Failed calls return structured
errors.

##### Community Notes Generation Prompts for Web-Search-Enabled LLMs.

The prompt for web-search-enabled LLM baselines is shown below.

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

### E.3 Evaluation Constraints

To ensure a fair and deployment-realistic evaluation, we impose the
following constraints on all applicable methods:

- •
  Temporal search restriction. Web search results are constrained to
  content available up to the timestamp of the human-written note,
  preventing access to future information.
- •
  Chronological memory access. For memory-based methods, episodes are
  processed in timestamp order, so each method can retrieve only
  experience accumulated from earlier episodes, i.e., note-generation
  trajectories for posts published earlier. This matches a practical
  streaming setting.

### E.4 EvoNote Variant Setup

We design the following three key variants of EvoNote to assess the
utility of memory and claim analysis:

- •
  EvoNote-fm (Frozen Memory): Allows retrieval from an existing memory
  bank but freezes the memory bank during evaluation. We use the
  earliest 5% of MM-HealthCN as warm-up data to initialize the memory
  bank. After each evaluation episode, no new planner or actor memory is
  distilled or stored. This ablation tests whether continual memory
  growth provides gains beyond retrieval from a fixed memory bank.
- •
  EvoNote-nm (No Memory): disables both memory retrieval and memory
  update, while keeping the rest of the pipeline unchanged, including
  instance-specific rubric planning, budgeted evidence seeking, and
  refinement. This tests whether memory contributes beyond the
  non-memory components of EvoNote.
- •
  EvoNote-nm-na (No Memory, No Analyzer): disables memory and
  additionally removes the instance-specific Claim Analyzer. The actor
  directly performs evidence seeking and note writing from the post
  representation. This tests whether explicit claim decomposition and
  verification planning improve note generation beyond a memory-free
  agentic pipeline.

### F.2 Applicability to “Needs More Ratings” (NMR) Cases

We further examine whether EvoNote can support Needs More Ratings (NMR)
cases, where crowd signals are still sparse and the helpfulness of
existing human notes has not yet been resolved. This setting complements
our main evaluation on MM-HealthCN, which focuses on cases with
crowd-resolved helpfulness labels. It also reflects a practically
important scenario for Community Notes: many posts require timely
correction before sufficient crowd consensus is available.

We construct an NMR evaluation set by selecting the most recent 300 NMR
cases before our data cutoff date, October 14, 2025, with an even
distribution across modalities: 100 Text, 100 Image, and 100 Video
cases. To test whether learned correction experience transfers to
unresolved cases, we run EvoNote with the evolving memory accumulated
from 1,200 samples in MM-HealthCN, and continue to obtain memory from
NMR cases in the note-generation process.

Table [8](#A6.T8 "Table 8 ‣ F.1 Length Compliance ‣ Appendix F Additional Results and Analysis ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")
shows that EvoNote remains effective on NMR cases. It produces helpful
notes for 82.0% of cases on average and achieves an 83.5% pairwise win
rate against the original human-written notes. The gains are consistent
across modalities, with especially large improvements in helpfulness
over human notes for Text and Video cases. These results suggest that
EvoNote can act as an early correction aid for posts awaiting community
consensus, using prior correction experience to generate timely and
helpful notes for cases that remain under-rated by the crowd.

### F.3 Evidence Use Analysis

This appendix details the evidence-use analysis in
§[7](#S7 "7 Discussion ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes").
Since health Community Notes are only useful when their corrections are
grounded in reliable and sufficiently contextualized evidence, we
evaluate not only whether a note cites sources, but also what kinds of
sources it cites and whether the cited evidence is diverse enough to
support cross-checking. We therefore measure evidence use along five
dimensions: source quality, domain diversity, semantic diversity,
average number of cited URLs, and multi-URL rate.

##### Source Quality.

We measure the credibility of cited evidence at the domain level. For
each note $`i`$, we extract all URLs, convert them to registrable
domains using eTLD+1, and deduplicate them into a domain set
$`\mathcal{D}_{i}`$. Each domain $`d`$ is mapped to a quality tier
$`\tau(d)\in\{1,2,3,4\}`$ using our maintained domain-tier table, with
unseen domains assigned to the lowest tier. Tier 4 includes official,
primary, or highly institutionalized sources, such as government
agencies, public-health organizations, authoritative medical resources,
and established fact-checking organizations. Tier 3 includes
peer-reviewed venues, medical databases, universities, research
institutes, teaching hospitals, and professional societies. Tier 2
includes mainstream news outlets, science media, reference sites,
preprint servers, and general nonprofit sources. Tier 1 includes unknown
sources, forums, blogs, marketing sites, user-generated-content
platforms, and other weakly verifiable sources. Representative examples
are shown in
Table [9](#A6.T9 "Table 9 ‣ Source Quality. ‣ F.3 Evidence Use Analysis ‣ Appendix F Additional Results and Analysis ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes").

| Tier | Domain      | Count |  Source Type            |
|------|-------------|-------|-------------------------|
| 4    | nih.gov     | 1,716 |  public health agency   |
| 4    | cdc.gov     | 1,349 |  government/regulator   |
| 4    | who.int     | 574   |  intl public health     |
| 3    | bmj.com     | 105   |  journal/publisher      |
| 3    | heart.org   | 47    |  professional society   |
| 3    | aap.org     | 46    |  professional society   |
| 2    | reuters.com | 380   |  news media             |
| 2    | bbc.com     | 292   |  news media             |
| 2    | apnews.com  | 229   |  news media             |
| 1    | x.com       | 192   |  social media platform  |
| 1    | youtube.com | 83    |  UGC/social platform    |
| 1    | reddit.com  | 60    |  UGC/social platform    |

Table 9: Representative examples by source-quality tier.

We convert each tier into a log-scaled quality score:

|     |                                          |     |
|-----|------------------------------------------|-----|
|     |
       ``` math
       q(d)=100\cdot\frac{\log\tau(d)}{\log 4}.
       ```                                       |     |

Thus, Tier 1–4 domains receive scores of $`0`$, $`50`$, $`79.25`$, and
$`100`$, respectively. The note-level source quality score is:

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
S_{\mathrm{src}}(i)=\begin{cases}\frac{1}{|\mathcal{D}_{i}|}\sum_{d\in\mathcal{D}_{i}}q(d),&|\mathcal{D}_{i}|>0,\\
0,&|\mathcal{D}_{i}|=0.\end{cases}
``` |  |

We report the dataset-level average:

|     |                                                                |     |
|-----|----------------------------------------------------------------|-----|
|     |
       ``` math
       S_{\mathrm{src}}=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}S_{\mathrm{src}}(i).
       ```                                                             |     |

##### Domain Diversity.

Source quality alone does not capture whether a note triangulates
evidence across independent sources. We therefore measure how evenly a
note distributes citations across domains. For each note $`i`$, let
$`\mathcal{U}_{i}`$ be the multiset of cited URLs with parsable domains,
$`n_{i}=|\mathcal{U}_{i}|`$, and $`p_{i}(d)=c_{i}(d)/n_{i}`$ the
citation distribution over domains. For notes with $`n_{i}\leq 1`$, we
set the score to 0. Otherwise, we compute normalized entropy:

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
S_{\mathrm{dom}}(i)=100\cdot\frac{-\sum_{d}p_{i}(d)\log p_{i}(d)}{\log n_{i}}.
``` |  |

This score reaches 100 when all cited URLs come from distinct domains
and decreases when citations concentrate on the same source. The
dataset-level score is averaged over notes with at least two effective
URLs:

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
S_{\mathrm{dom}}=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{I}_{\geq 2}|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{I}_{\geq 2}}S_{\mathrm{dom}}(i),\quad\mathcal{I}_{\geq 2}=\{i:n_{i}\geq 2\}.
``` |  |

##### Semantic Diversity.

Domain diversity may still overestimate evidence breadth when different
sources repeat the same information. We therefore measure semantic
diversity among cited evidence pages. For each note $`i`$, we embed the
extracted content of each cited URL using jinaai/jina-embeddings-v3. Let
$`\mathcal{E}_{i}=\{\mathbf{e}_{i1},\ldots,\mathbf{e}_{iM_{i}}\}`$
denote valid evidence embeddings. If $`M_{i}<2`$, we set the score to 0.
Otherwise, we compute the average pairwise cosine distance:

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
S_{\mathrm{sem}}(i)=100\cdot\frac{2}{M_{i}(M_{i}-1)}\sum_{1\leq a<b\leq M_{i}}\frac{1-\cos(\mathbf{e}_{ia},\mathbf{e}_{ib})}{2}.
``` |  |

Higher scores indicate that cited evidence is less semantically
redundant. The dataset-level score is averaged over notes with at least
two valid evidence embeddings:

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
S_{\mathrm{sem}}=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{I}_{\geq 2}|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{I}_{\geq 2}}S_{\mathrm{sem}}(i),\quad\mathcal{I}_{\geq 2}=\{i:M_{i}\geq 2\}.
``` |  |

##### Average URLs and Multi-URL Rate.

We also report two citation-coverage metrics. For each note $`i`$, let
$`u_{i}`$ be the number of extracted URL citations. The average number
of cited URLs is

|     |                                                  |     |
|-----|--------------------------------------------------|-----|
|     |
       ``` math
       \mathrm{AvgURLs}=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}u_{i}.
       ```                                               |     |

The multi-URL rate measures the fraction of notes that cite at least two
URLs:

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathrm{MultiURLRate}=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\mathbb{I}[u_{i}\geq 2].
``` |  |

Together, these metrics quantify whether a method grounds notes in
external evidence and how often it supports a correction with multiple
sources.

| Model | Source Quality | Domain Diversity | Semantic Diversity | Avg. URLs | Multi. URL Rate |
|----|----|----|----|----|----|
| Human Notes | 61.68 | 90.04 | 21.59 | 2.03 | 40.83 |
| Grok-4.3 | 65.55 | 91.47 | 15.75 | 1.83 | 68.42 |
| CrowdNotes+ | 65.32 | 90.50 | 16.60 | 1.97 | 68.92 |
| ExpRAG | 70.63 | 87.80 | 20.73 | 1.08 | 12.42 |
| EvoNote | 72.93 | 93.32 | 22.56 | 1.97 | 68.92 |

Table 10: Evidence quality and diversity of EvoNote vs. representative
baselines on MM-HealthCN. We compare cited evidence across source
quality, domain diversity, semantic diversity, average cited URLs, and
multi-URL rate. Metric formulations are detailed in
§[F.3](#A6.SS3 "F.3 Evidence Use Analysis ‣ Appendix F Additional Results and Analysis ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes").

##### Results.

Table [10](#A6.T10 "Table 10 ‣ Average URLs and Multi-URL Rate. ‣ F.3 Evidence Use Analysis ‣ Appendix F Additional Results and Analysis ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")
and
Figure [5](#S7.F5 "Figure 5 ‣ 7 Discussion ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")
show that EvoNote achieves the strongest overall evidence profile among
representative baselines. It obtains the highest source quality score,
domain diversity, and semantic diversity, while matching the strongest
multi-URL rate and maintaining nearly the same average number of cited
URLs as human notes and CrowdNotes+. This indicates that EvoNote does
not improve evidence use by simply citing more URLs. Instead, it
retrieves stronger sources and combines less redundant evidence,
suggesting that evolving experience memory helps the agent learn when to
seek primary sources, verify source-claim alignment, and broaden the
evidence context.

### F.4 Memory Utility Analysis

We further analyze the evolving experience memory to understand what
reusable strategies EvoNote learns from its own correction trajectories.
This analysis complements
§[3](#S3 "3 Motivating Analysis: Reusable Misinformation Correction Experience ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")
by examining the composition of Note Writer memories, i.e., memories
used during evidence acquisition and note writing.

Across MM-HealthCN, EvoNote accumulates 4,277 memory items, each
associated with an action phase and a reusable strategy. To characterize
these memories, two human annotators collaboratively reviewed 200
sampled memory items and constructed an attribution taxonomy. We then
use GPT-4.1 to classify the remaining memory items by their primary
attribution category.
Table [12](#A6.T12 "Table 12 ‣ F.4 Memory Utility Analysis ‣ Appendix F Additional Results and Analysis ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")
reports the resulting distribution and category descriptions.

The learned memories concentrate on concrete correction operations. For
evidence acquisition, the largest categories are primary or
official-source verification, causal overgeneralization checks,
evidence-quality assessment, and domain-specific verification. For note
writing, the dominant categories involve safe next-step guidance,
practical health implications, contextualization, and uncertainty
calibration. These patterns show that EvoNote does not merely store past
cases; it distills recurring correction failures into phase-specific
strategies that can guide later evidence seeking and note framing.

|  Failure Category |  Example Pattern | Count | % |  Repairability |  System Consequence |

|  Ungrounded final answer |  {"action":"write", "support":\[\]} | 36 | 57.1 |  Not repairable; required evidence is absent |  Rejected due to missing evidence URLs |
|  Length-control failure |  Valid {"text": ..., "reason": ...} but output remains too long | 18 | 28.6 |  Not repairable without regenerating content |  Cannot produce platform-compliant note |
|  Residual schema mismatch |  Missing reason, missing action, or missing discriminator | 6 | 9.5 |  Partially repairable in principle, but unresolved here |  Rejected by schema validation |
|  Runtime timeout |  httpx.ReadTimeout | 3 | 4.8 |  Not applicable |  Episode interrupted |
|  Total failed runs |  – | 63 | 100.0 |  – |  – |

for more detailed analyses.

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
| Attribution | Ratio |  Description |
| Evidence Acquisition Stage |  |  |
| PRIMARY_OFFICIAL_VERIFICATION | 21.0% |  Verify concrete factual, policy, legal, governmental, electoral, regulatory, or official-action claims using primary or authoritative sources. |
| CAUSAL_GENERALIZATION | 20.4% |  Check whether the post improperly generalizes from anecdotes, single incidents, isolated cases, correlations, or temporal associations to causal or population-level conclusions. |

### F.5 Case Study: Retrieved Memory Guides Regulatory-Process Verification

Figure [11](#A6.F11 "Figure 11 ‣ F.5 Case Study: Retrieved Memory Guides Regulatory-Process Verification ‣ Appendix F Additional Results and Analysis ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")
illustrates how retrieved experience improves a concrete correction
trajectory. The flagged post frames COVID-19 vaccines as “experimental,”
which requires checking the regulatory process behind EUA and full
approval. The representative baselines: human-written note, Grok-4.3,
CrowdNotes+, and ReMem, give broadly correct rebuttals, but they either
remain generic or cite sources that do not directly explain the specific
EUA/approval distinction.

In contrast, EvoNote retrieves a memory triggered by claims about
vaccines being “experimental” or improperly tested. The memory directs
the agent to verify clinical-trial phases, EUA versus full approval, and
safety/efficacy review. Guided by this strategy, EvoNote cites FDA
evidence and writes a more targeted note explaining that COVID-19
vaccines underwent Phase I–III trials and met FDA safety and efficacy
standards for EUA/approval. This case shows how phase-specific memory
can turn prior correction experience into better evidence seeking and
more precise public-facing correction.

![Refer to caption](2606.02215v1/case-study.png)

Figure 11: Case study: memory-guided regulatory verification. Retrieved
experience helps EvoNote verify clinical-trial, EUA, and safety-review
details for a stronger correction. See detailed analysis in
§[F.5](#A6.SS5 "F.5 Case Study: Retrieved Memory Guides Regulatory-Process Verification ‣ Appendix F Additional Results and Analysis ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes").

### F.6 Captioning Enables More Reliable Agentic Medical Reasoning

We analyze captioning as an enabling step for reliable multimodal
health-note generation. Agentic generation of health Community Notes
requires two capabilities at once: (1) accurate interpretation of visual
health-related content and (2) reliable multi-step agentic behavior for
search, source visiting, evidence synthesis, and length-constrained
writing. Recent studies show that current VLM agents remain brittle in
long-horizon decision settings, with challenges in visual grounding,
planning, and action execution [Koh et al. (2024)](#bib.bib38); [Xie et
al. (2024)](#bib.bib37); [Paglieri et al. (2025)](#bib.bib35); [Jandial
et al. (2025)](#bib.bib36). This motivates our design: use
human-validated captioning
(§[C.3](#A3.SS3 "C.3 Caption Quality Validation ‣ Appendix C MM-HealthCN Benchmark Details ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes"))
to preserve correction-relevant visual content, then rely on
medical-capable LLMs (in our case, MedGemma-27B) for evidence-seeking
reasoning.

We test this choice on 400 Image cases of MM-HealthCN by directly
instantiating EvoNote with the multimodal version of MedGemma-27B. The
caption-based LLM pipeline completes all cases with platform-compliant
outputs, whereas the direct VLM pipeline frequently fails to produce
valid note-generation trajectories. Even after automatic repair
heuristics, 63 runs remain invalid. As shown in
Table [11](#A6.T11 "Table 11 ‣ F.4 Memory Utility Analysis ‣ Appendix F Additional Results and Analysis ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes"),
the dominant failures are ungrounded final answers with missing evidence
URLs, length-control errors, schema mismatches, and runtime timeouts.
These failures arise before reliable helpfulness judgment can even be
applied, showing that valid agentic execution is itself a bottleneck for
direct VLM deployment.

Among the cases where the VLM pipeline produces valid outputs,
Figure [6](#S7.F6 "Figure 6 ‣ 7 Discussion ‣ Better with Experience: Self-Evolving LLM Agents for Evidence-Grounded Health Community Notes")
shows that it still underperforms the caption-based LLM pipeline and
even falls below the no-memory LLM variant. These results support
caption-based instantiation as a more reliable design for this setting:
human-validated captions retain the visual claim context, while
medical-capable LLMs provide stronger tool use, evidence acquisition,
and calibrated note writing.

## Appendix G LLM Usage Statement

We used LLMs in this work for three purposes: note generation within the
proposed framework, automated evaluation under the protocols described
in the paper, and light language polishing of the manuscript. All
experimental design choices, data analysis, result interpretation,
claims, and final writing decisions were made and verified by the
authors. The authors take full responsibility for the content of the
paper, including the correctness of reported results and the validity of
the conclusions.
````
